title: Model variant evaluation framework: sequential testing, shadow mirroring, and automated rollback
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Define and deliver a reproducible A/B-style evaluation framework for model variants that combines staged canary rollouts, shadow traffic comparisons, and automated rollback triggers. The framework must let product and infra teams configure exposure schedules, pre-register primary and secondary metrics, and run sequential statistical checks (early stopping and safety gates) while preventing peeking and false positives.
context_background: We currently have ad-hoc canary processes: engineers deploy a variant and manually route traffic. This leads to inconsistent safety coverage, delayed detection of regressions, and manual rollback decisions. As model churn increases and customers rely on predictable inference behavior, we need a standardized experiment orchestration layer that integrates with Redwood Console, routing, and monitoring, while remaining safe for high-throughput production workloads.
proposal: Build a product-facing orchestration that allows teams to declare: (1) variant groups (control/candidate), (2) exposure schedule (ramp percentages, mirror-only phases), (3) pre-registered metrics with directionality and weights, and (4) statistical policy (sequential/Bayesian checks, min sample size, false-discovery control). The system will execute experiments, evaluate signals in real time, surface dashboards, and perform automated rollback when defined safety conditions are met.
rollout_strategy: Phased integration: Phase A - API and internal beta enabling shadow mirroring and manual ramps; Phase B - automated sequential checks with alerting and soft-fail notifications; Phase C - automated rollback and integration with infra canary primitives for full traffic routing control. Provide per-route controls, tenant-scoped limits, and a default conservative policy for enterprise customers.
statistical_checks: Implement sequential analysis methods to support interim looks without inflating Type I error: options include alpha-spending group sequential tests, Bayesian credible intervals with ROPE thresholds, and stopping rules based on minimum effect size and power. Provide default conservative settings plus an advanced mode exposing parameters. Include corrections for multiple metric testing (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR) and a requirement for pre-registration of primary metric(s).
metrics_and_signal_processing: Define signal pipeline: raw event ingestion -> normalization (per-customer weighting) -> smoothing/windows (exp. weighted) -> drift detection. Support composite scores composed of weighted primary/secondary metrics (latency P95, token cost per call, response quality score, hallucination rate). Allow teams to attach custom validators (e.g., n-gram overlap for semantic fidelity) and specify guardrail thresholds.
monitoring_and_alerting: Auto-provision dashboards in Redwood Console for every run (traffic, metric deltas, cumulative effect, p-values/Bayes factors). Default alerts: metric regression beyond configured tolerance, traffic saturation issues, divergence between mirrored and live requests, and sustained resource pressure. Alerts must include run context and links to runbook and rollback toggle.
acceptance_criteria: PM and ENG can create a variant run via API or Console specifying exposures, metrics, and check policy
System mirrors shadow traffic for the new variant without affecting user-visible latency in mirror phases
Sequential checks evaluate metrics in real-time and surface clear decision signals (pass/warn/fail) in Console
Automated rollback triggers can be configured and executed end-to-end in a test environment (manual approval optional)
Dashboards and logs for each run are generated and include links to related PRs and evaluation artifact storage
The framework includes a safety default policy preventing >5% initial exposure for high-risk customers unless explicitly overridden
tasks: Spec: detailed API contract and Console UX mockups
ENG: mirror routing and low-latency shadow path implementation (ENG-3241)
ENG: sequential stats engine and threshold evaluator (ENG-4120)
DX: Console views for run creation, status, and per-metric drilldown
Security: review data retention and KMS use for experiment artifacts
QA: simulated runs including synthetic regressions, and runbook playthroughs
Docs: how-to, recommended metric catalogs, and pre-registration templates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: premature rollout due to noisy early signals -> Mitigation: require minimum sample size and deploy conservative default alpha-spend
Risk: increased cost from mirroring traffic -> Mitigation: limit mirror rate by default and provide chargeback metrics
Risk: false discovery from multiple metrics -> Mitigation: default FDR correction and enforce a single pre-registered primary metric for automated rollback
Risk: rollback flapping across automated and manual controls -> Mitigation: cooldown windows and human approval gates for enterprise plans
notes: Design decision: prioritize safety and reproducibility over aggressive early exposure. We will expose advanced statistical knobs only to teams that pass an onboarding checklist (understanding of sequential testing). Future extension: integrate offline power calculators and synthetic signal replay to simulate worst-case regressions before live traffic.
